analyst_view.overall: Early view: an important game for the play-off places, with Torreense 19th on 6 points and Celtic 32nd on 3 after finally winning, 3-2 against Besiktas. Both defences have struggled in Europe, with Torreense's games averaging four goals and Celtic's more than four, although Martin O'Neill's side top the Scottish Premiership.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean higher: Torreense's four games have produced 16 goals and Celtic's 17, with Celtic conceding 11. Torreense are without Jorge Aguirre (sent off against Ararat) and played at Leiria rather than their own small ground, but neither defence has given much reason to expect a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, a high figure that fits two sides who attack more than they defend. With both needing points, I see no reason to move away from it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. Celtic's European games have been open rather than physical and Torreense came back against Ararat by attacking, not by fouling, so I stay with a low-ish count.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, split almost evenly. That matches two open sides with weak defences.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean a little higher: games with this many goals usually come with plenty of efforts on target, and Celtic's substitutes Camilo Duran and Callum Osmand changed the Besiktas game by running straight at goal.
